The *Pañcakapuggalapaññatti* (Pp 2.5) constitutes the fifth section of the *Puggalapaññatti*, the third book of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Following the numerical schema of the work, it defines and classifies various types of persons (*puggala*) grouped into sets of five [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral notes an explicit thematic link with the *Ārabhatisutta* (AN 5.142) of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya*, which similarly treats fivefold categories of individuals [SuttaCentral].
Textual reuse analysis underscores the close genetic relationship between this Abhidhamma text and the Sutta Piṭaka. According to DharmaNexus, the *Pañcakapuggalapaññatti* shares 2,059 passages with 95 other Pali texts, overwhelmingly matching the *Pañcakanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 5; 641 matches totaling over 99,000 characters, including the extended sequence §11.3–22.1 aligned with AN 5.75) [DharmaNexus]. Significant internal reuse is also recorded with the *Catukkanipāta* (AN 4), *Dasakanipāta* (AN 10), *Tikanipāta* (AN 3), the preceding chapter *Catukkapuggalapaññatti* (Pp 2.4), and major discourses such as the *Sāmaññaphala Sutta* (DN 2) and *Mahātaṇhāsaṅkhaya Sutta* (MN 38) [DharmaNexus].
